parsed.doc_summary: MA G.L. c. 40P § 4 generally bars cities and towns from enacting, maintaining or enforcing rent control, with a narrow voluntary, municipally-compensated exception. This means no local rent cap in Boston or Cambridge.

rules.conflict_note: State bar on local rent control; may preempt conflicting local rent control ordinances in Boston and Cambridge. Effective date not stated in the document (known to stem from 1994 ballot Question 9).
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all cities and towns in Massachusetts.
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not state an effective date.
rules.exemptions: A city or town that accepts the chapter may adopt voluntary rent control that is compensated from general funds, applies only to owners of ten or more rental units, to units with fair market rent of $400 or less, and excludes regulation of occupancy, services, evictions, condo conversion.
rules.interaction: Prohibits local rent control, so no municipal rent caps apply.
rules.key_value: Statewide ban on local rent control
rules.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that provides:
rules.requirement: Massachusetts cities and towns may not enact, maintain or enforce rent control. A narrow exception allows only voluntary, municipally-compensated regulation of larger owners' low-rent units.
rules.title: State prohibition on local rent control

no_rule_findings.finding: State law bars municipalities from enacting or enforcing rent control, so Boston has no local rent cap.
